relations.myth: Brujos ride the sea-horse to board the Caleuche
relations.note: The sea-horse transports brujos to the vessel, carrying as many as twelve.

relations.myth: Pincoya delivers drowned mariners to the Caleuche
relations.note: Pincoya conveys drowned bodies aboard, where the ship revives them.

relations.myth: Pincoy helps carry the drowned aboard
relations.note: Pincoy assists Pincoya in transporting drowned mariners to the vessel.

relations.myth: Sirena Chilota helps carry the drowned aboard
relations.note: She assists Pincoya and Pincoy in conveying drowned mariners to the vessel.
Some late accounts identify the sea ruler as the vessel’s creator.

relations.myth: Millalobo governs access to the Caleuche
relations.note: Some late accounts make Millalobo its maritime superior and rule-giver.
Grouped dolphins indicate pursuit by the Caleuche; later lore personifies its herald.

relations.myth: Huenchur orders Cahuelche to announce the Caleuche
relations.note: Huenchur commands the Cahuelche whose leaps herald the vessel.
